observation_summary: The StrBuilder.contains(char) and indexOf(char) methods were incorrectly iterating over the entire underlying buffer length instead of the current size of the string builder, leading to false positives when searching for characters that existed in the buffer but were logically removed.
hypothesis: The methods contains(char) and indexOf(char) use the wrong loop termination condition (thisBuf.length instead of this.size), causing them to scan beyond the valid data stored in the StrBuilder.
prediction: Changing the loop termination condition from 'thisBuf.length' to 'this.size' will correctly restrict the search to the active portion of the buffer.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the loop termination condition in both 'contains' and 'indexOf' was changed from 'thisBuf.length' to 'size'. This confirms that the iteration logic was flawed because it ignored the logical size of the string builder.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic algorithmic error where the loop termination condition is incorrect. It is not a missing guard (Checking) because the logic itself is fundamentally flawed in its iteration strategy. It is not an Assignment/Initialization issue because the variables themselves are correct; the loop logic is what is wrong. Therefore, it fits the Algorithm/Method category.
evidence_used: The fix diff shows the loop condition changed from 'i < thisBuf.length' to 'i < this.size'.
The bug report states: 'StrBuilder contains usages of thisBuf.length when they should use size'.
The failing test 'testLang295' confirms that the method is looking beyond the end of the string.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a condition, it is not a guard or validation check; it is the loop termination logic itself, which is part of the algorithm's traversal strategy.
The issue is not about the value assigned to a variable, but the logic of the loop control flow.
